newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Lula gets election nod from former rival.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Lula gets election nod from former rival.

text.p: The runner-up in Brazil's last two presidential elections, Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, took a step closer on Wednesday to running next year as the left's single candidate when a former rival backed him.

"When one reaches my age, one is duty bound to help consolidate and strengthen the leadership of Lula, not just for personal reasons, but for the Brazilian people who need him," said veteran left-winger Leonel Brizola.
Brizola was the most prominent opponent to Brazil's 1964-85 military dictatorship and runs the Democratic Labour Party. Lula is a former factory worker and a founder of the Workers Party.
In 1989 and 1994, they both ran for president, splitting the left-wing vote.

However, Brizola, who once called Lula a "bearded toad," said Brazil's various socialist and communist parties needed to back one candidate if they were to frustrate President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's 1998 re-election plan.

Lula declined to declare his candidacy but did not rule himself out either. "What we must do now is discuss a policy programme, discuss with our allies and then we can choose the candidate," he told reporters.

Brazil holds presidential, congressional and state governorship elections in October 1998. For the first time, a sitting president will be allowed to run again after Cardoso pushed a bill through Congress allowing re-election.
